speaker: Kimi K3
text: ICICI Bank's 12.6% five-year CAGR with 22% earnings growth and a 0.53 PEG makes it the highest-quality compounder in Indian financials, and at 4.6% off highs it's offering a rare entry point. The ₹10k budget buys 7 shares at ₹2,405; round-trip delivery on Zerodha is ₹38.15 (0.38%) plus 20% STCG tax if held under a year, so you need roughly 1.2% gross just to break even after all costs. For auto and battery exposure within your ₹10k: Tata Motors at ~₹780 gets 12 shares, Exide at ~₹320 gets 31 shares, Amara Raja at ~₹1,100 gets 9 shares — all whole shares only. On the US side, $100 fractional lets you own slices of TSLA ($240), ALB ($95), or FREYR ($2) without lot-size drag, but penny battery names carry binary risk. The IPO route remains closed — US bookbuilds need accredited status, Indian IPOs need ₹15k minimum lot.
